turns.question: At which hour of the day were the most page views recorded between 20 September and 3 October 2026, and how many page views were in that hour?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no page-view-per-hour metric and no hour time grain, so I cannot give the peak hour or its count. The closest metric is site_sessions (site sessions with a page view), which is counted per day only.

turns.question: What was the median time in hours between an outreach message and the partner's reply, for messages sent between 1 and 3 October 2026?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no median reply-time metric. The closest metrics are messages_replied (outreach messages that got a reply, by the day sent) and reply_rate (the share of messages that got a reply), and neither measures time to reply.

turns.question: What share of candidates who applied in September 2026 reached the interview stage or beyond?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no metric for the share of applicants who reached interview or beyond. The closest metrics are applications (candidates who applied, by the day they applied) and candidates_in_stage (candidates in each hiring stage at the end of each day), and neither gives that share.

turns.question: What was the median number of days from application to hire for candidates hired in September or October 2026?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no median days-to-hire metric. The closest is time_to_hire_days (Time to hire, days), which is an average of days from applying to being hired, so it does not answer the median question.

turns.question: How many degrees Celsius warmer was Istanbul than Amsterdam on average in daily temperature on 1 and 2 October 2026?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no weather or temperature metric, so I cannot compare Istanbul with Amsterdam for 1 and 2 October 2026. None of its metrics covers daily temperature.

turns.question: What was the total ad spend in EUR per non-cancelled order placed in September 2026?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no ad-spend-per-order metric. The closest metrics are ad_spend_eur (ad spend in EUR, by day) and orders_total (all orders placed, cancelled included), and it does not divide one by the other.

turns.question: How many delivery-topic customer service calls were there per 100 shipped orders in September 2026?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no calls-per-100-shipped-orders metric. The closest are calls_labelled (calls labelled by topic, a model-derived label, where delivery is a topic) and orders_total filtered to the shipped status, and no rate combines them.

turns.question: What was the median order amount in EUR for non-cancelled orders placed in September 2026?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no median order value metric; median_order_value_eur is listed as not available in this dialect. The closest is average_order_value_eur (the average amount of a non-cancelled order), which is not a median.

turns.question: What was the 90th percentile order amount in EUR for all orders placed between 17 August and 2 October 2026?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no 90th-percentile order metric. The closest are average_order_value_eur and revenue_eur (the sum of non-cancelled order amounts), and neither is a percentile.

turns.question: How many customers placed more than three orders between 17 August and 2 October 2026?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no metric that counts customers by number of orders above three. The closest is repeat_customers, which counts customers with a non-cancelled order in the period who have placed two or more orders in all, a different threshold.

turns.question: For customers whose first order was placed in October 2026, what was the median number of days between their signup date and that first order?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no median days-to-first-order metric. The closest is signup_to_first_order_rate, the share of customers whose first order came within 30 days of signing up, which is a rate and not a number of days.

turns.question: Between 17 August and 10 October 2026, how much higher in EUR was the average non-cancelled order amount of customers who signed up before 2026 than that of customers who signed up in 2026?
turns.answer: Customers who signed up in 2024, the only pre-2026 signup year with orders in this period, averaged 102.67 EUR per non-cancelled order, against 41.00 EUR for customers who signed up in 2026, over orders placed 17 August to 10 October 2026.
